name: Sannomiya
tagline: Kobe's buzzing central transport and shopping hub
description: The beating heart of Kobe, where every train line converges and the Motomachi arcades, department stores, coworking spaces and restaurants cluster. It is the most convenient base, with the mountains a short walk north and the waterfront just south of the tracks.
bestFor: Nomads wanting maximum convenience, transport links and after-work dining on the doorstep
cons: Busier and noisier than the suburbs

name: Kitano
tagline: Historic foreign quarter on the hillside
description: The atmospheric slope above Sannomiya where Kobe's old foreign residences, the ijinkan, still stand among cafes and boutiques. Steep, leafy lanes and Western-style mansions give it a cosmopolitan, storybook feel, with fine city views and a slower, elegant pace.
bestFor: Character seekers who love period architecture, quiet cafes and hillside strolls near the centre

name: Harborland and Meriken
tagline: Waterfront district with parks and views
description: Kobe's redeveloped bayfront, taking in Meriken Park, the Port Tower and the Harborland shopping and entertainment complexes. It is a bright, open area of sea air, promenades and dining, especially atmospheric after dark when the harbour lights come on.
bestFor: Those who want sea views, evening strolls and a modern, spacious feel by the bay

name: Nada and Okamoto
tagline: Residential sake and university district east
description: The calmer eastern stretch toward the university areas, home to the Nada sake breweries and the leafy Okamoto neighbourhood. Quieter and more local than the centre, it mixes student cafes, everyday shops and easy commuter access along the Hankyu and JR lines.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting quieter local life, lower rents and a genuine neighbourhood feel
pros: More affordable rents than the centre
Good cafes and sake heritage nearby
